# Going further: optical receivers, BER and sensitivity {#sec-receivers} [![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/{{< var github_user >}}/{{< var repo >}}/blob/main/{{< var subdir >}}/notebooks/receivers.ipynb){.colab-link}  Run this chapter's code in Google Colab (no installation). *This chapter is not in the slides. It connects the noise analysis of @sec-noise and @sec-apd-noise with the bit-error rate of Ch. 2 and the optical amplifiers of Ch. 4, and answers the question every link designer asks: how many photons does one bit need?* ## Key relations A digital receiver decides, bit by bit, whether a "1" or a "0" was sent by comparing the photocurrent with a threshold. With on–off keying (OOK) the "1" gives a mean current $I_1$ with noise $\sigma_1$ and the "0" gives $I_0$ with noise $\sigma_0$. For Gaussian noise and the optimum threshold, the **bit-error rate** depends only on the **Q factor** (Ch. 2): $$ Q=\frac{I_1-I_0}{\sigma_1+\sigma_0},\qquad \text{BER}=\frac12\operatorname{erfc}\!\left(\frac{Q}{\sqrt2}\right),\qquad \text{BER}=10^{-9}\Leftrightarrow Q=6,\quad 10^{-12}\Leftrightarrow Q=7.03 . $$ The **sensitivity** is the average optical power $\bar P=(P_1+P_0)/2$ that gives the target BER. With $P_0=0$, a photodiode of responsivity $\mathcal R$ and an electrical bandwidth $B_e\approx R_b/2$ for a bit rate $R_b$: - **pin, thermal-noise limited** ($\sigma_0=\sigma_1=\sigma_T$, the noise of the load or TIA): $\bar P=Q\sigma_T/\mathcal R$. It grows as $\sqrt{B_e}$ and is independent of the photon energy. - **pin, shot-noise limited** (ideal amplifier): $\bar P=Q^2eB_e/\mathcal R$, i.e. $Q^2/2\approx18$ photons per bit for $\eta=1$ at BER $10^{-9}$ (with $B_e=R_b/2$). - **APD**: the signal is multiplied by $M$, the thermal noise is not, and the shot noise gets the excess factor $F$; there is an optimum $M$ (@sec-apd-noise). - **Optically preamplified** (EDFA + pin, Ch. 4): the amplifier gain $G$ lifts the signal far above the thermal noise; the noise is now the beat between the signal and the amplified spontaneous emission, $\sigma^2_{s\text{-}sp}=4\mathcal R^2GP_1S_{sp}B_e$, with $S_{sp}=n_{sp}(G-1)h\nu$, plus the ASE–ASE beat in the optical bandwidth $B_o$. - **Quantum limit**: an ideal photon counter makes an error only when a "1" produces no photoelectron at all, with probability $e^{-N_1}$. $\text{BER}=\frac12e^{-N_1}$ gives $N_1=20$ photons in a "1", i.e. **10 photons per bit** on average at BER $10^{-9}$. ## Live panel: sensitivity of four receivers ```{ojs} //| echo: false import {berQ, qe, h, c0, mcintyre} from "./det_sim.js" viewof rv = Inputs.form({ ber: Inputs.select(new Map([["10⁻³ (with FEC)", 1e-3], ["10⁻⁹", 1e-9], ["10⁻¹²", 1e-12]]), {value: 1e-9, label: "target BER"}), wl: Inputs.range([0.8, 1.6], {value: 1.55, step: 0.01, label: "wavelength (µm)"}), eta: Inputs.range([0.3, 1], {value: 0.72, step: 0.01, label: "detector QE"}), inoise: Inputs.range([0.5, 50], {value: 10, step: 0.5, label: "amplifier input noise (pA/√Hz)"}), k: Inputs.range([0, 1], {value: 0.5, step: 0.01, label: "APD ionisation ratio k"}), NF: Inputs.range([3, 8], {value: 5, step: 0.1, label: "EDFA noise figure (dB)"}), Bo: Inputs.range([12.5, 200], {value: 50, step: 2.5, label: "optical filter bandwidth (GHz)"}), Rb: Inputs.range([0.1, 100], {value: 10, step: 0.1, label: "bit rate (Gb/s), B_e = R_b/2"}) }) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false rvOut = { const Q = (() => { let lo = 0, hi = 12; for (let i = 0; i < 80; i++) { const m = (lo + hi) / 2; if (berQ(m) > rv.ber) lo = m; else hi = m; } return (lo + hi) / 2; })(); const wl = rv.wl * 1e-6, hv = h * c0 / wl, R = rv.eta * qe / hv, G = 1000; const sens = (Rb) => { const Be = Rb / 2, sT = rv.inoise * 1e-12 * Math.sqrt(Be); const pin = (2 * qe * Be * Q * Q + 2 * Q * sT) / (2 * R); let apd = Infinity, Mopt = 1; for (let i = 0; i <= 300; i++) { const M = 10 ** (2.5 * i / 300), F = mcintyre(M, rv.k), p = (Q * Q * 2 * qe * F * M * Be + 2 * Q * sT) / (M * R) / 2; if (p < apd) { apd = p; Mopt = M; } } const nsp = 10 ** (rv.NF / 10) * G / (2 * (G - 1)), S = nsp * (G - 1) * hv, Bo = rv.Bo * 1e9; const s0 = Math.sqrt(4 * R * R * S * S * Bo * Be + sT * sT + 2 * qe * R * S * Bo * Be); let lo = -18, hi = -1; for (let i = 0; i < 80; i++) { const m = (lo + hi) / 2, P1 = 10 ** m, I1 = R * G * P1; const s1 = Math.sqrt(s0 * s0 + 4 * R * R * G * P1 * S * Be + 2 * qe * I1 * Be); if (I1 / (s1 + s0) > Q) hi = m; else lo = m; } const pre = 10 ** hi / 2, ql = -Math.log(2 * rv.ber) / 2 * hv * Rb; return {Rb, pin, apd, Mopt, pre, ql}; }; const sweep = d3.range(0, 61).map(i => sens(1e8 * 1000 ** (i / 60))); const pts = sweep.flatMap(s => [{Rb: s.Rb / 1e9, P: 10 * Math.log10(s.pin / 1e-3), c: "pin + amplifier"}, {Rb: s.Rb / 1e9, P: 10 * Math.log10(s.apd / 1e-3), c: "APD (optimum M)"}, {Rb: s.Rb / 1e9, P: 10 * Math.log10(s.pre / 1e-3), c: "EDFA + pin"}, {Rb: s.Rb / 1e9, P: 10 * Math.log10(s.ql / 1e-3), c: "quantum limit"}]); return {Q, cur: sens(rv.Rb * 1e9), pts, hv}; } Plot.plot({ width: Math.min(width, 1050), height: 320, x: {label: "bit rate (Gb/s)", type: "log"}, y: {label: "sensitivity (dBm)", grid: true}, color: {legend: true, domain: ["pin + amplifier", "APD (optimum M)", "EDFA + pin", "quantum limit"], range: ["#e34948", "#eda100", "#2a78d6", "#0b0b0b"]}, marks: [Plot.line(rvOut.pts, {x: "Rb", y: "P", stroke: "c", strokeWidth: 2}), Plot.ruleX([rv.Rb], {stroke: "#52514e", strokeDasharray: "4,3"})] }) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false html`
Q = ${rvOut.Q.toFixed(2)} · at ${rv.Rb} Gb/s (photons per bit = P̄/(hν Rb)):
pin: ${(10 * Math.log10(rvOut.cur.pin / 1e-3)).toFixed(1)} dBm (${(rvOut.cur.pin / (rvOut.hv * rv.Rb * 1e9)).toFixed(0)} photons/bit) · APD at M = ${rvOut.cur.Mopt.toFixed(1)}: ${(10 * Math.log10(rvOut.cur.apd / 1e-3)).toFixed(1)} dBm (${(rvOut.cur.apd / (rvOut.hv * rv.Rb * 1e9)).toFixed(0)}) · EDFA + pin: ${(10 * Math.log10(rvOut.cur.pre / 1e-3)).toFixed(1)} dBm (${(rvOut.cur.pre / (rvOut.hv * rv.Rb * 1e9)).toFixed(0)}) · quantum limit ${(10 * Math.log10(rvOut.cur.ql / 1e-3)).toFixed(1)} dBm (${(-Math.log(2 * rv.ber) / 2).toFixed(1)})
` ``` Things to try: the pin line has slope 5 dB per decade (thermal noise ∝ $\sqrt{B_e}$), the quantum limit 10 dB per decade (fixed photons per bit). The pin receiver is 20–35 dB above the quantum limit at all rates, because the thermal noise of even a good amplifier corresponds to thousands of photons per bit. Lower the amplifier noise to 1 pA/√Hz: the pin improves by 10 dB. Set $k=0$ for the APD: it gains another 9 dB, because the gain becomes almost noiseless ($F o2$). The preamplified receiver is within 9–14 dB of the quantum limit almost independently of the electronics; narrowing the optical filter towards the signal bandwidth helps. Lowering the BER target to $10^{-3}$ (with forward error correction, the norm today) halves Q and saves about 3 dB for the thermal-noise-limited pin. ## Worked comparison at 10 Gb/s, 1550 nm ::: {#tbl-rx .cell tbl-cap='Sensitivity of 10 Gb/s receivers at BER = 10⁻⁹ (Q = 6), 1550 nm, QE = 0.72 (R = 0.9 A/W), B_e = 5 GHz, amplifier noise 10 pA/√Hz, APD with k = 0.5, EDFA with G = 30 dB, NF = 5 dB, B_o = 50 GHz.' execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} Q, Rb, wl = dl.q_from_ber(1e-9), 10e9, 1.55e-6 Be, R = Rb/2, dl.responsivity(0.72, wl) sT = 10e-12*np.sqrt(Be) hv = dl.h*dl.c0/wl pin = dl.sensitivity_pin(Q, R, Be, i_amp=sT) Ms = np.logspace(0, 2.5, 400) apd_all = np.array([dl.sensitivity_apd(Q, R, Be, M, dl.excess_noise_mcintyre(M, 0.5), i_amp=sT) for M in Ms]) iapd = np.argmin(apd_all) pre = dl.sensitivity_preamp(Q, R, Be, 50e9, 1000, 5.0, wl, sT) Nql, Pql = dl.quantum_limit(1e-9, wl, Rb) shot = Q**2*dl.qe*Be/R rows = [("pin + TIA (thermal + shot)", pin), (f"APD, optimum M = {Ms[iapd]:.0f}", apd_all[iapd]), ("EDFA + pin", pre), ("ideal pin, shot noise only", shot), ("quantum limit (photon counting)", Pql)] pd.DataFrame([(n, f"{10*np.log10(p/1e-3):.1f} dBm", f"{p*1e9:.2f} nW", f"{p/(hv*Rb):.0f}") for n, p in rows], columns=["receiver", "sensitivity", "P̄", "photons per bit"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

The curves are steep: 1 dB more power lowers the BER by orders of magnitude, the 'waterfall' of receiver measurements.](receivers_files/figure-html/fig-ber-output-1.png){#fig-ber width=755 height=391} ::: ::: ## Why it matters: the link budget Ch. 2 computed the attenuation of a fiber; Ch. 4 the launch power of a laser. The receiver sensitivity closes the budget: $P_\text{launch}-\alpha L-\text{penalties}\ge\bar P_\text{sens}$. With 0 dBm launched, 0.2 dB/km and 3 dB of margin, the 10 Gb/s pin receiver above reaches about 100 km, the APD about 150 km, and the preamplified receiver about 180 km (before dispersion, Ch. 2, becomes the limit). Long-haul links put amplifiers every 80 km instead, and their accumulated ASE, not the receiver, sets the OSNR (Ch. 4). ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Going further - **Coherent detection.** Mixing the signal with a strong local oscillator $P_{LO}$ on the photodiode gives a beat current $2\mathcal R\sqrt{P_sP_{LO}}$ that can be made far larger than the thermal noise; the receiver becomes shot-noise limited by the LO. Show that the SNR then approaches $\eta P_s/(h\nu B)$ and that heterodyne PSK needs about 18 photons per bit for BER $10^{-9}$. Coherent receivers with balanced photodiodes and DSP carry 400–800 Gb/s per wavelength today. - **Photon counting at the quantum limit.** Deep-space optical links (NASA's DSOC on Psyche, 2023) use superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors and pulse-position modulation to reach ~1 photon per bit or less. Why can PPM beat the 10 photons/bit of OOK? - **Non-Gaussian statistics.** The APD gain and the ASE beat noise are not Gaussian; the Gaussian Q approximation overestimates the required power for APDs (McIntyre distribution) by about 1 dB. - **Extinction ratio penalty.** If the "0" carries a power $P_0=rP_1$ (laser biased above threshold, Ch. 4), the thermal-limited sensitivity degrades by $(1+r)/(1-r)$. Compute the penalty for $r=0.1$. ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Complements - G. P. Why is it worse than the quantum limit of 10? 2. In the panel, at what bit rate do the pin and APD sensitivities become equal for $k=0.5$? Explain why APDs lose their advantage at low bit rates with a quiet amplifier. 3. A 25 Gb/s PON receiver must reach −28 dBm at BER $10^{-3}$. Which receiver type do you need? 4.
